heading.en: Business at the speed of a click

hook.en: You can buy a book, pay a bill, sell old furniture and order a meal without leaving your room. E-business has changed how firms and customers meet.

objectives.en: Describe the scope of e-business: B2B, B2C, C2C and intra-B
Explain online transactions, payments and security concerns

narration.en: You can buy a book, pay a bill, sell old furniture and order a meal without leaving your room. E-business has changed how firms and customers meet.

body.en: E-business is the conduct of business activities (trade, production, finance, human resources, communication) using computer networks and the internet. E-commerce is the part of e-business that covers buying and selling online. Its scope: B2B (business to business, such as a car maker buying parts online), B2C (business to customer, online shopping), C2C (customer to customer, selling used goods on an online marketplace), C2B (customers offering services to firms), and intra-B (within a firm, linking departments). Benefits: easy formation, low cost, convenience, speed, global reach and support for a paperless society.

title.en: On the board: steps of an online purchase

text.en: Register on the site; browse; add to cart
Choose delivery address and check the order
Cash on delivery, cards (debit/credit), net banking,
Order confirmed; goods packed and shipped
Tracking; delivery; returns and refunds if needed

narration.en: Let us build up steps of an online purchase on the board, one step at a time.

text.en: A furniture maker orders wood from a supplier's portal
You order shoes from an online store
A student sells an old cycle to another person on a classifieds site
Staff in two branches of a bank share files on the company network
A retailer restocks from a wholesaler's app
A family books train tickets online

explanation.en: Who sells to whom decides the category: firm to firm, firm to customer, customer to customer, or inside one firm.

body.en: E-business lacks personal touch, has delays in delivery of physical goods, faces people's resistance and low digital skills in some places, and raises security concerns: transaction risks (default on order, delivery or payment), data theft, identity theft, phishing and hacking, and the threat to privacy. Safeguards include encryption, secure (https) websites, two-factor authentication, strong passwords, trusted payment gateways and reading reviews before buying.

problem.en: Distinguish e-business from traditional business on four points.

steps.en: Formation: e-business is easy and cheap; traditional needs premises and licences.
Physical presence: not needed online; needed for traditional shops.
Reach: global and round the clock online; local and in fixed hours traditionally.
Personal touch: low online; high in a traditional shop.

answer.en: E-business is easier, cheaper and wider in reach but less personal.
